items.title: Two CultureMech recipes are both named gyps_medium — the GYPS link's uniqueness was never checkable
items.body:
Surfaced by the hardened matcher in #489, running against the real recipe tree. Not a defect in that PR — the link is correct — but a live ambiguity the old tooling structurally could not show.

## Two recipes, one name

```
CultureMech:002799  data/normalized_yaml/bacterial/gyps_medium.yaml
  original_name: GYPS MEDIUM
  Glucose, Yeast extract, Peptone, Sea Salt, MES

CultureMech:009837  data/normalized_yaml/bacterial/TOGO_M450_GYPS_Medium.yaml
  original_name: GYPS Medium
  Distilled water, Yeast extract, MES, Sea salts (Sigma), Glucose, Peptone, N2
```

Same core formulation from two sources; 009837 additionally lists water and an N2 atmosphere.

## Why this matters

MIM's `GYPS` record links to **CultureMech:002799**, and that choice is defensible — its evidence reads *"CultureMech additionally lists MES and Sea Salt and no starch"*, which describes 002799's five ingredients exactly. So the verification was done against that record and the link is right.

**But its uniqueness was never checked, and could not have been.** The old matcher indexed recipes in a one-value dict keyed on lower-cased name, so only one of the two `gyps_medium` recipes was ever visible; the curator saw whichever happened to be indexed last. That the surviving one was the correct one is luck, not process.

Now that the index is multi-valued, `GYPS` reports as ambiguous with both ids, which is the honest state.

## What to decide

Is `CultureMech:009837` a **duplicate** of 002799 (a CultureMech-side dedup, in #218/#219's neighbourhood) or a **distinct variant** worth its own record? If the latter, MIM's `GYPS` may warrant a second reference — the schema added in #489 supports `VARIANT_OF` for exactly this.

No change to the existing link is proposed here: `culturemech_reference.medium_id` already names 002799 unambiguously, which is the whole point of carrying an id rather than a name.

## Scale

This is one instance of a general condition: **2291 CultureMech names are shared by more than one recipe**, and `defined_freshwater_medium_cocl2` names 29. Any future link verified by name has the same exposure; the ambiguity flag in `reports/culturemech_link_candidates.tsv` is what makes it visible.

items.title: Triage the 71 records asserting a mapping their own research report advised against
items.body:
## Finding

`scripts/validate_records_against_research.py` (#309) compares each ingredient
record against the deep-research report for that same ingredient. Over the 527
records researched so far it found **71 `STATUS_CONFLICT`s** — the record asserts
an ontology mapping while its own report recommended `UNMAPPED`.

**Every one of them was written by the same mechanical sweep,
`promote_resolved_unmapped`.** That is the #203/#263 pattern recurring: a
plausible identifier promoted by a mechanism that never decided anything.

## Important caveat — do not treat all 71 as defects

The Edison/PaperQA3 lane cannot open an ontology page. Its reports say so
verbatim ("no ChEBI CURIE was verified in the retrieved evidence"), so it
defaults to "retain UNMAPPED" whenever it cannot confirm a term — which is most
of the time. An Edison "retain UNMAPPED" on its own is therefore weak evidence.

That is exactly why the second (Claude) lane exists, and it already resolved 22
of these: `LANE_DISAGREEMENT_RESOLVED` marks a conflict the Claude lane cleared
by resolving the term Edison could not. Those 22 need no action.

## Triage order

Work `mappings/record_research_validation.md`, most severe first:

1. **17 `BOTH_LANES_DISPUTE`** — both independent lanes dispute the mapping.
   Strongest signal in the ledger; start here.
2. **`P1 CURIE_REFUTED`** — a report names the record's exact CURIE and argues
   against it. The quoted line usually names the right term.
3. **`P1 VERDICT_REFUTES`** — a per-field verdict table refutes an identity
   field and supplies a corrected value.
4. The remainder of the `STATUS_CONFLICT`s, checking `promoted_by` and
   `documented_rationale`.

Each row carries the quoted report line that produced it, so most are a one-read
decision: keep with a written justification, downgrade `mapping_quality`, or
demote.

## Note on coverage

The ledger currently covers 527 of 2,841 records; the Edison sweep is ongoing
(~30 records/hour, account-capped). Re-run the validator as it completes — these
counts will grow.

items.title: Cooked_Meat_Medium keeps FOODON:03305103 (the food) as its identity: the mint is blocked by two mixtures whose component references are pinned by the resolution component ledger
items.body:
Deferred from #312 batch 3 (registry mints).

`data/ingredients/mapped/Cooked_Meat_Medium.yaml` is Robertson's cooked meat medium (MediaDive ingredient 1824, complex compound; Oxoid CM0081), a formulated anaerobe medium. Its identifier is `FOODON:03305103 "meat (cooked)"`, a food, from a 2026-05-01 `fuzzy-top` auto-upgrade: the medium was grounded to one of its parts. The verified correction (Section 3 step 3 / Section 6): mint `kgmicrobe.ingredient:cooked_meat_medium` with `FALLBACK_REGISTRY` and no FOODON identity, close or broad row, the `Artificial_Sea_Salt` shape.

It cannot land yet. Two mixtures reference the food through this record:

- `Modified_Cooked_Meat_Medium.yaml` and `Fastidious_Anaerobe_Broth_With_Meat_Granules.yaml` each carry `components[0] = {component_name: "meat (cooked)", component_id: FOODON:03305103, reference_scope: MIM_CATALOG}`. Once no active record holds FOODON:03305103, `qc-component-partonomy` (required) fails with `UNRESOLVED_MIM_REFERENCE`, and the right fix is `reference_scope: EXTERNAL_TERM` (the part *is* the FOODON food term).
- But both mixtures are pinned byte-for-byte: `reports/semantic_review_20260921/resolution/components/dispositions.tsv` (`SEM:6028aad55b495239163c`, `current_record_sha256`) makes `build_review.py` fail with `Stale component disposition`, and `reports/sssom_completion_20260921/mapping_review/nonmapping_cohorts.json` carries SUPPORTED approvals for their registry rows keyed to the owner hash, which `assemble_review.py` refuses to restamp.

Same family as #740 (identity-plan pin) and #745 (position-bound holds): a completed review pins records so that a later, verified, unrelated correction cannot be applied. Needed: a supersedable link for component-scope changes on the resolution side (the `mapping_changes/` receipts already do this for the completion side), and the assembler should withhold, not raise, when a cohort-approved owner is touched by a receipt.

Until then the record and the two component references stay as they are; `SOURCE_LABEL_IDENTIFIER_OVERRIDES` entries for the two "Cooked meat medium" source labels should be added with the mint.

Related: #312, #740, #745, #710.

items.title: Label-index answers still wrong or missing for CultureMech recipe labels (pin-refresh replay)
items.body:
## Source

Found while refreshing CultureMech's vendored MIM label index to `6643131b`. I replayed every recipe label in CultureMech's occurrence table through the old and new pins; the method is from CultureBotAI/CultureMech#417. The pin refresh is a large improvement overall (99% of rows unchanged, and the changes are mostly hydrate-specific corrections). These are the labels where MIM's **current** answer still looks wrong or missing. In each case the old answer was no better, so none of this blocks the pin.

## Wrong form

| CultureMech label | recipe rows | resolves to | problem |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `MnSO4・xH2O` (+ `MnSO4·nH2O`) | 61 | CHEBI:86364, `MnSO4 x 1 H2O` | A variable hydrate resolves to the monohydrate. The variable-sulfate precedent (#646 and others) gives these a local `x n H2O` identity. |
| `NiCl2 x H2O`, `NiCl2・H2O` | ~5 | CHEBI:53542, nickel(II) chloride hexahydrate | A monohydrate label resolves to the hexahydrate. |
| `Trisodium citrate x 3 H2O` | 2 | CHEBI:53258 | A trihydrate label resolves to a non-trihydrate term. |
| `Potassium phosphate` | 4 | CHEBI:63036 | A generic label resolves to one specific potassium phosphate salt. |

The NaH2PO4 monohydrate spellings that resolve to the dihydrate record (~36 rows) are already tracked as #758.

## Missing or ambiguous

- **`sodium nitrate`, 58 rows, unresolved:** ambiguous because the stock-solution record `Sodium nitrate (0.70 M stock)` (`kgmicrobe.ingredient:sodium_nitrate_~28070_m_stock~29`) carries the bare compound name as a synonym next to CHEBI:63005. A stock solution's record shouldn't claim the compound's name.
- **`α-Ketoglutarate`, 3 rows, now unresolved:** #232 correctly retired it from the disodium-salt record as `REJECTED_LABEL`, but no record now claims the anion or acid name.
- **`Sea Salt`, now unindexed:** the old pin had it ambiguous through two `ontology_label` rows. Either way it got no identity, but no record claims generic sea salt.

The full replay table is in the CultureMech pin-refresh PR description.

## More from the CultureMech#537 review (same replay)

- **`MgSO4 x H2O` (12 rows) and `MgSO4 . H2O` (1) → CHEBI:31795, magnesium sulfate *heptahydrate*.** These resolve as trusted `mim_exact` through a REJECTED tombstone row on `Mgso47h2o.yaml` that carries the monohydrate label. Under the old pin they were flagged ambiguous; now they're confidently wrong, and KGX emits the edge.
- **`Na2MoO4.H2O`, `Na2MoO4 . H2O`, `Na2MoO4 · H2O` (3 rows) → CHEBI:75213, the *dihydrate*,** by the same tombstone-row pattern.
- **`sodium glutarate` (1 row): a regression.** It used to resolve to `cas:13521-83-0` (disodium glutarate). MIM no longer indexes that `ontology_label`, so CultureMech falls back to the recipe's local CHEBI:24329, the glutarate anion: a salt collapsed onto its parent.
- **NaH2PO4 monohydrate spellings split:** `NaH2PO4•H2O` → CHEBI:114249 (the monohydrate), while `NaH2PO4 x H2O` / `·H2O` go to the dihydrate record (#758). Two spellings of one substance get different identities.

Root pattern for the first two: merge tombstones keep raw labels naming a *different hydrate* than their survivor, and the label index publishes them as REJECTED rows that consumers follow by contract.

## From the unified-mapping fix (culturebotai-claw#571)

- **`MgSO .7H O` (17 occurrences)** is a safe (`unique`) synonym on the *anhydrous* Magnesium sulfate record (CHEBI:32599), but it's a garbled heptahydrate label. Its recipes carry the correct heptahydrate CHEBI:31795. Now that the unified mapping follows MIM's label index, this MIM synonym placement decides the published identity.
- **`Na2HPO4·7H2O`** has no label-index row; only other spellings of the heptahydrate are indexed. So its recipes' anhydrous CHEBI:34683 still wins (MIM#808).

## From the claw#571 review: MIM record and synonym defects that now decide unified-mapping identities

| label (occurrences) | MIM's `unique` answer | problem |
|---|---|---|
| `DL-Tryptophan` (4) | record `DL-Tryptophan` on CHEBI:57912 | CHEBI:57912 is the L-tryptophan zwitterion, so the racemate is recorded as an enantiomer |
| `Na2-DL-malate`, `Sodium DL-malate`, `Na-DL-malate` and others (26) | `Sodium malate`, CHEBI:91261 | DL labels sit on a disodium (S)-malate identity |
| `Na2SiO3` (8) | synonym on `Na2SiO3 x 9 H2O` (CHEBI:132108) | an anhydrous formula label on the nonahydrate |
| `Magnesium Chloride` (5) | record `Magnesium chloride` = CHEBI:86345 | a generic name owns the hexahydrate identity |
| `MgSO .7H O` (17) | synonym on anhydrous `Magnesium sulfate` | a garbled heptahydrate label (noted above) |

## From the second claw#571 review

- **Sodium malate family** (`Sodium malate` 14, `Sodium DL-malate` 11, `Na2-DL-malate` 6, `Na-malate` 6, `Na malate` 4, `Na-DL-malate` 4, `DL-Na-malate` 3, `DL-Sodium malate` 2; 50 occurrences): MIM's `Sodium malate` record sits on CHEBI:91261, disodium **(S)**-malate, while the labels are racemic or stereo-unspecified. The recipes carry CHEBI:91260 (disodium malate).
- **`H3BO2`** (3): an unreviewed import record grounds this (likely a typo for H3BO3, boric acid) to boronic acid CHEBI:38267.


## Update 2026-10-14 (second review of #881)

**Fixed in #881:**
- `MgSO4 x H2O`, `MgSO4 . H2O` and `MgSO4・H2O` now resolve to the monohydrate `cas:14168-73-1` (#893).
- `MgSO .7H O` now resolves to the heptahydrate CHEBI:31795 (#899).

**Still open, same class, from the label index on #881's head:**

Damaged-subscript formula labels resolving to the anhydrous form or to a different compound:

| label | `label_index.csv` answer | CultureMech recipe rows |
|---|---|---:|
| `CaCl .6H O` | CHEBI:3312, anhydrous CaCl2 | 5 |
| `ZnCl .6H O` | CHEBI:49976, anhydrous ZnCl2 | 3 |
| `EDTA.Na .2H O` | CHEBI:64734 (`Na2-EDTA`) | 3 |
| `CoCl .6H O` | CHEBI:35696, anhydrous CoCl2 | 0 |
| `FeSO .7H O` | CHEBI:75832, anhydrous FeSO4 | 0 |
| `LiCl.H O` | CHEBI:48607, anhydrous LiCl | 0 |
| `NaH PO .2H O` | CHEBI:37585, anhydrous NaH2PO4 | 0 |
| `ZnSO .7H O` | CHEBI:86463 (`AlK(SO4)2`), a different compound | 0 |
| `Na SiO .9H O` | CHEBI:86463 (`AlK(SO4)2`), a different compound | 0 |

Water-ratio names resolving to a different hydrate:
- `cobalt(2+) sulfate--water (1/7)` → CHEBI:53470, anhydrous CoSO4;
- `Cobalt(II) chloride--water (1/7)` → CHEBI:53503, the hexahydrate.

**Consistency question, not an explicit contradiction:** `Mgso4_X_7_H2o` carries four names, all ChEBI related synonyms of CHEBI:32599:
- `magnesium sulphate`;
- `magnesium(II) sulfate`;
- `sulfuric acid magnesium salt`;
- `sulphate of magnesia`.

They resolve to the heptahydrate, while `Magnesium sulfate` resolves to the anhydrous form. Semantic-review finding SEM:f345b845583ac48792ef is open on this.

items.title: ingredient_type is unset on 98% of the microbedecoder cohort (511/520)
items.body:
## Finding

`ingredient_type` is unset on **559 of 2,497** mapped records (22%), and the
distribution is not diffuse — it is one cohort:

| cohort | unset | total | |
|---|---|---|---|
| microbedecoder import | **511** | 520 | **98%** |
| everything else | 48 | 1,977 | 2% |

The 2026-08-04 microbedecoder import appears to write no `ingredient_type` at
all, and `AUTO_CLASSIFY_INGREDIENT_TYPE` never ran over that cohort. Records
from other paths carry it normally.

## Why it is load-bearing, not cosmetic

`ingredient_type` is what would let downstream logic distinguish three states
that currently look identical — an empty `chemical_properties` block:

- **empty because it is a mixture** — `Artificial_Sea_Salt`, a branded
  formulation with no structure to record;
- **empty because the term is a structure-free class** — `Ascorbate`, correctly
  on the bare-name anion class, where copying `L-ascorbate`'s structure in would
  be a *defect*;
- **empty and genuinely fillable** — `Ascomycin`, where CAS 104987-12-4 and a
  full structure are available from ChEBI.

Without it, any enrichment pass that treats "empty" as "needs filling" will
corrupt the middle group while fixing the third. That is the root confusion
behind #316, and it makes this a prerequisite for widening enrichment rather
than an independent cleanup.

A second symptom: the few microbedecoder records that *do* carry a value can
carry a stale one. `Catalase` has `ingredient_type: SINGLE_INGREDIENT` with the
recorded reason "(CHEBI primary)" — but it has had no CHEBI primary since the
June 2026 repair moved it to NCIT.

## Suggested action

Run `AUTO_CLASSIFY_INGREDIENT_TYPE` over the microbedecoder cohort, and add the
classifier to the import path so the next ingest does not reproduce the gap.

Note the classifier has its own coverage hole worth fixing at the same time: it
recognises `infusion` as a complex-material pattern but has no `serum` rule,
which is why `Brain_Heart_Infusion` is classified `UNDEFINED_MIXTURE` while its
sibling `Bovine_Calf_Serum` is unset. Worth sweeping
serum/plasma/extract/digest/hydrolysate.

Query that sizes it: records with a `CREATED_AS_UNMAPPED` event dated
2026-08-04 and no `ingredient_type`.

Related: #316, #322.

items.title: 25 identifier sets publish the same ingredient label under two or more records
items.body:
Found while triaging the CultureMech unresolved residual. Evidence table:
`reports/culturemech_ambiguous_identifiers.tsv` (written by
`scripts/triage_culturemech_residual.py`).

55 CultureMech surface forms (383 recipe mentions) fold onto a MIM label that **two or
more records publish**. CultureMech fails closed on an ambiguous `label_index` row, so
each of these is an unresolvable ingredient — and unlike a plain miss, it cannot be fixed
by adding a spelling, because the question "which record owns this name?" has no answer
yet.

Ranked by affected mentions:

| mentions | identifier set |
|---:|---|
| 141 | `MICRO:0001647` / `NCIT:C75874` (Sea Salt) |
| 95 | `FOODON:03315719` / `mesh:C017721` (Casamino acids) |
| 34 | `MICRO:0000460` + 5 `kgmicrobe.ingredient:*` vitamin solutions |
| 28 | `FOODON:03315719` / `MICRO:0000182` (Pancreatic digest of casein) |
| 19 | `CHEBI:17439` / `CHEBI:176843` (Vitamin B12) |
| 14 | `CHEBI:3312` / `CHEBI:86158` (CaCl2 2H2O) |
| 14 | `CHEBI:91247` / `kgmicrobe.ingredient:l-cysteine_x_hcl_x_h2o_solution` |
| 10 | `CHEBI:31795` / `CHEBI:32599` (MgSO4 7H2O) |
| 5 | `CHEBI:35696` / `kgmicrobe.compound:cocl2_x_2_h2o` / `cocl2_x_4_h2o` |
| 3 | `CHEBI:17909` / `CHEBI:26833` (sulfur) |

These are not all one defect. At least three kinds are mixed here, and they want different
answers:

1. **Duplicate records on one substance** — `Sea Salt`, `Casamino acids`. A merge under the
   `merge-ingredients` skill.
2. **Granularity disagreement** — `CHEBI:17909` (sulfur atom) vs `CHEBI:26833` (elemental
   sulfur); `CHEBI:17439` (cyanocobalamin) vs `CHEBI:176843` (cobalamin). A decision under
   MAPPING_SEMANTICS Section 3, not a merge.
3. **A wrong synonym on a hydrate sibling, which is an identity error rather than an
   ambiguity.** `CoCl2 6H2O` matches records for the **di**- and **tetra**-hydrate, so
   those records carry a hexahydrate spelling they do not denote. Same shape for
   `CaCl2 2H2O` against `CHEBI:3312`, which is anhydrous calcium chloride. Hydration state
   is identity (MAPPING_SEMANTICS Section 3): these synonyms should be removed regardless
   of how the ambiguity is resolved.

Kind 3 is the one worth doing first -- it is a wrong claim now being published, whereas
kinds 1 and 2 are unresolved questions.

Not addressed in the grounding PR that found this: resolving these needs per-family
judgement, and the PR deliberately skips every shared identifier rather than picking an
owner arbitrarily.
